Slow noise (the 1/f band of the draw, the hyperfine field) is quasi-static: a Gaussian offset averaged by Gauss–Hermite quadrature, which gives the exp(−(τ/T₂)²) envelope with T₂ = √2 ħ/σ_E exactly; no Monte Carlo at runtime, so the output is a deterministic function of the draw. The g-factors are a seeded draw (SpinDraw); dg/dV, the hyperfine rms, T₁ and the Markovian T_φ are placeholders (calibration: none) until the Step 6 entries are confirmed.
  • Pauli spin blockade (spin.psb): the singlet's (0,2) occupation steps at the anticrossing (√2 t matrix element, thermal average with the upper branch), the triplet's at ε = E_V of the receiving dot; the contrast is the window; the visibility multiplies in the triplet's survival exp(−t_int/T₁). The sensor's own charge-readout error (Step 4) is a separate factor for the consumer.
  • Not yet: three-qubit cost, EDSR/micromagnet driving terms, the spin-funnel, Elzerman readout, CPMG noise spectroscopy and the J-versus-Ramsey check (second Step 6 PR), J-gate fidelity.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Easier: the fingerprint, house cells, J(ε), J(V_B), ESR lines, Rabi, Ramsey and the PSB window all follow from one device's draws; the fingerprint visibility and the Ramsey T₂* change with the noise draw, the PSB window with the valley draw, the ESR splitting with the g draw.
  • Harder: quasi-static averaging ignores the spectral shape within the band (CPMG will need the spectrum itself); the Lindblad step cost grows as 4ⁿ for n spins.
  • Must now: P0 tests for the perturbative limit, trace and positivity, Rabi, Ramsey, T₁, the PSB window and the draw dependence; protocols exchange-vs-detuning, exchange-vs-barrier, exchange-fingerprint, exchange-house-cells, esr-line, rabi-chevron, ramsey-fringes, psb-readout-window.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Heitler–London or Hund–Mulliken J from orbitals — a compile-tier solver; the Hubbard sector is exact for the two-site model phantom already uses and costs one 6×6 diagonalisation.
  • Monte Carlo over noise traces at runtime — rejected for cost and reproducibility; quadrature over a quasi-static Gaussian is exact for the envelope and deterministic. Trace-based noise returns for CPMG.

docs.title: 0022 — Blockade transport as sequential cycles with a spin-branch average; the funnel as two-level mixing; Elzerman shots as exponential draws; noise spectroscopy by filter functions on the draw's spectrum; gate fidelity as the entanglement fidelity of the Lindblad channel
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-26 Step: 6

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The second half of Step 6 needs transport with Pauli blockade, the spin funnel, single-shot readout traces, charge-noise spectroscopy with the qubit, and a gate fidelity that reacts to the device's draws (the step's exit criterion), all within rule 4's cost and rule 3's reproducibility.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Bias triangles (spin.blockade): sequential tunnelling through the electron and hole cycles at the (1,1)/(0,2) vertex, each cycle's current e / (¼ τ_S + ¾ τ_T) with τ the sum of inverse rates of its steps; lead steps carry Fermi factors from the constant-interaction energies, the interdot step is downhill-allowed with a thermal tail; the triplet branch passes only beyond E_V (the valley-excited (0,2) triplet) or through a mixing rate quenched by field as 1/(1 + (B/B_mix)²); reverse bias starts from the (0,2) singlet and has no blockade. Not a master equation over all states: ADR 0017's rate equation covers zero-bias dynamics; a finite-bias master equation with spin is a later cost decision.
  • Funnel (spin.mixing): S–T₋ and S–T₀ as two-level anticrossings with time-averaged transfer ½ Δ²/(Δ² + δ²); the mixing Δ is a placeholder; ΔE_Z from the g draw; J from spin.exchange.
  • Elzerman (spin.elzerman): shots as exponential draws in a fixed order (deterministic per seed); the analytic empty-probability curve is the ensemble limit and a P0 test.
  • Noise spectroscopy (spin.noise_spectroscopy): W_N = exp(−∫ S_ω F_N/(2πf)² df) with the CPMG filter function evaluated numerically on a log grid; the spectrum is the draw's 1/f law with the amplitude defined over the sensor band and extended above it, so the qubit and the sensor share one amplitude; projection through dJ/dε and the lever arms.
  • Gate fidelity (spin.gates): entanglement fidelity of the propagated Lindblad superoperator against the target unitary (which includes the nominal J and the g draw's Zeeman difference), averaged over the quasi-static detuning offset by quadrature; F_avg = (dF_e + 1)/(d + 1).
  • EDSR (spin.dynamics): the drive strength ½ g μ_B (dB/dx) x_ac with a dipole displacement estimate; a placeholder until a micromagnet layout exists.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Easier: the exit criterion holds — the SWAP fidelity varies with the noise draw and the readout visibility with the valley draw; the CPMG spectrum and the sensor PSD are one draw.
  • Harder: the blockade picture has no co-tunnelling, no excited orbital lines and constant inelastic rates; the funnel is time-averaged; three-qubit cost stays open.
  • Must now: P0 tests for each (blocked base, lifting by E_V and by mixing, no reverse blockade; funnel position; shot average; Ramsey, echo and CPMG limits and the white-noise invariance; perfect gate without noise, degrading with σ_ε, sweet spot); protocols psb-bias-triangles, spin-funnel, elzerman-trace, charge-noise-spectroscopy-cpmg, charge-noise-spectroscopy-j-vs-ramsey, exchange-gate-fidelity.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• A finite-bias master equation with spin states for the triangles — correct but heavier; deferred.
  • Monte Carlo over noise traces for CPMG — the filter-function integral is exact for Gaussian noise and deterministic.

docs.title: 0023 — A compiled device is a parameter record in its own layer; the basis is recomputed, not stored; JSON serialisation; the FEM backend is a hook; optimum reads the record
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-26 Step: 7

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR 0001 promised a compile() that runs every expensive draw and derivation once and a Device the runtime layers consume without a solver. Plan §8 left two decisions open: which external solver to wrap (#1) and how to serialise a device (#3). Rule 2 says nothing imports compile, yet optimum must read a compiled device.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• A device layer (phantom.device) between spin and optimum holds the Device record and the builders of every runtime object (CI model, sensor, barrier, Hubbard model, rate equation, sensed double dot with the noise draw, spin draw). compile writes it; optimum and consumers read it; the layer order in rule 2 and scripts/check_imports.py gains device.
  • What compile_device does, in order: scenario draw (charges, misalignment, wiring, noise) → basis on the clean grid with the draw applied → programmed point mapped through the wiring faults → dots, sensor and CI model from the basis with the sensor gate moved onto its peak's flank → barriers to the leads and between the dots at the tunnelling level, their WKB transmissions by the action integral along the cut (electrostatics.barrier_action, which follows the barrier's shape instead of the rectangular height × width estimate, so t(V_B) is smooth) → the interdot t ≈ ħω₀ √T / π and the barrier gate's exponential scale from two nearby evaluations → valley splittings from the dots' radii → g-factors. Every draw takes a sub-seed derived from the device seed.
  • Serialisation (plan §8 #3): JSON, sorted keys, one entry per line, floats at full precision, with a format_version and the model version of every layer that produced the device; the basis grid is not stored, Device.basis() recomputes it deterministically from the layout and the draw. A device file is a few kilobytes and diffs line by line.
  • Backends (plan §8 #1 stays open): closed_form is the only one; fem is a hook behind the [fem] extra that raises with the open decision's name until a solver is chosen. Everything downstream of the basis is backend-agnostic.
  • optimum reads the record and answers per layer: sensor flank by a coarse scan and a fine scan of |dI/dV|, the answer a grid point (a golden-section search and a parabolic interpolation both differed between platforms); the virtual-gate matrix from the inverse of the plunger block of the lever-arm matrix scaled to the raw plungers' lever arms, with cross-talk compensation for the other gates and the sensor gate holding the sensor potential fixed; the barrier voltage for a target t from the compiled exponential; the Pauli-blockade read point from the receiving dot's valley draw and the Elzerman peak time from the compiled lead rate; the exchange sweet spot in the operating cell (the symmetric point shifted by whole electrons to the cell the device sits in), its T₂* and SWAP fidelity with the device's noise. Brute force attains each (P0).
  • Screening: still absent from the closed-form basis; it is the FEM backend's job (plan §8 #1), not a runtime approximation.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Easier: one call compiles a device; one file carries it; every runtime object comes from it; the layer rule stays checkable.
  • Harder: a tenth layer. The rectangular WKB estimate of ADR 0017 remains only as the bound in readout.rates and its P0 limits; the Step 4 dynamics protocols moved to the action integral (readout.wkb_rate_from_action_hz) in the second Step 7 PR, with two operating points shifted so their pictures keep the same rate-times-dwell regimes.
  • Must now: P0 round trip (text-identical after reload; identical stability map from the reloaded device), the clean device bit-identical to the Step 2 derivation, optimum attained by brute force; protocols compiled-device-roundtrip, virtual-gates-map, optimum-sensor-flank.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Storing the basis grid in the device (hundreds of megabytes per device) — rejected; recomputation is deterministic and takes well under a second for the closed form.
  • Pickle or NPZ — rejected: not diffable, not versioned by construction.
  • Letting optimum import compile — rejected: rule 2's "nothing imports compile" is what keeps the offline tier out of every consumer's runtime.

docs.title: 0024 — The consumer contract: one import surface above compile, a session with a forward clock, truth apart from what a user may see, a contract test consumers run, a checked surface snapshot, and 0.x releases
docs.text: Status: Accepted (release tagging amended by 0025) Date: 2026-10-27 Step: 8

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR 0003 promised consumers plan §4 (compile, Device.at, Device.measure, Device.truth, optimum), a contract test the qdt adapter also runs, and a changelog. Step 7 built the compiled Device and optimum but no runtime surface with time: runtime_sensed() hands out the migrated qdt-sim core, which a consumer would have to drive, seed and clock itself. qdt's Analysis 0007 (issue #40) found six gaps between the planned surface and what its adapter needs: the sensor bias in sense, a noise seed apart from the device seed, holding voltages without reading, a statement of what one sample is, truth under the names a tune-up recovers, and the line between knowable fields and truth. Rule 2 said nothing imports compile, yet a consumer's one import has to reach compile_device.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• One import surface. phantom.api re-exports every name a consumer uses (compile_device, CompileParams, Device, State, Session, Measurement, SpinOutcome, Truth, SensorTruth, Knowable, optimum and its parts, the layout types, ValleyParams, SpinParams, DEVICE_FORMAT_VERSION, __version__) and adds model_versions(). phantom.api and phantom.contract sit above compile: they may import every layer, contract imports api, and no layer or root module imports either (rule 2 amended; scripts/check_imports.py).
  • The runtime surface lives in device (device.session, device.truth), so it reads the record and the layers below and never compile. Device.at(v, v_sd) is the noise-free State, vectorised. Device.session(noise, dynamics, charge, noise_seed) is a Session with a clock that only moves forward: sense(v, dwell_s, samples, v_sd) reads each point at the end of each dwell, sample k at t₀ + (k+1)·dwell; hold(v, duration_s) keeps the gates at v and evolves the charge there; wait(duration_s) holds at the last point; spin_readout samples the PSB readout of a prepared pair as a protocol step (voltage-driven spin is #41). Device.measure is a fresh session's sense.
  • What one sample is, fixed per session: charge="sampled" (default) puts one charge state in the sensor per sample, the state of a Markov jump trajectory of the rate equation (from the present state, the next is drawn from the column of exp(W·dwell)) with dynamics=True, an independent Boltzmann draw (qdt-sim's behaviour) without; charge="mean" puts ⟨N⟩ in, propagated or thermal. The noise processes are sampled at each sample's time; the white floor keeps the draw's density at 1 ms (σ ∝ √(1 ms / dwell)). A hold samples the gate noise once at its start.
  • Seeds. The device seed is the device's identity. noise_seed=None replays the device's own noise realisation, so identical calls on two fresh sessions are identical; an integer replaces only the noise draw's realisation seed (a hash of both seeds) and keys the session's charge and spin streams, keeping every noise parameter.
  • Knowable and truth. Device.knowable() is what a user may be shown: material, gate names, layout, temperature, programmed point, sensor, barrier and reservoir gates. Everything else on a Device is truth, including the seed and operating_point_v (it holds the compiled sensor set point). Device.truth() gathers it under the quantities a tune-up recovers: the charge lattice in electrons per programmed volt (through the wiring matrix) and the sensor peak in programmed sensor-gate volts (peak, period, charging energy, lever arm, width, the wing at atanh(1/√3) widths and the linear- response sensitivity there at a given bias), so qdt's adapter only renames.
  • Contract test. phantom.contract.run(device) checks every promise above on a device; python -m phantom.contract [device.json ...] runs it on the reference device and on each file, exit status 0 or 1. phantom's CI runs it (tests/test_contract.py); qdt's CI runs it on the pinned tag and its committed device files.
  • Surface snapshot. scripts/api_surface.py writes docs/api/surface.json (every public name, its signature, dataclass fields, public methods); check_all.sh fails when the surface differs from it, so an API change is a reviewed diff with a CHANGELOG.md entry.
  • Releases. Semantic versioning in 0.x: the minor version rises for any breaking change to the surface or to DEVICE_FORMAT_VERSION, the patch version otherwise; a change of output for the same parameters, seed and calls bumps the module's MODEL_VERSION and is listed in the changelog. The owner tags releases (v0.2.0 first); how often phantom releases and qdt moves its pin is the owner's open decision (Step 8).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Easier: qdt's adapter becomes renaming and plumbing over Session (its hold/sense protocol maps one to one); a consumer gets a new noise realisation on the same committed device; truth and the knowable fields are stated by phantom, not re-derived by a consumer; an API change cannot slip in unreviewed.
  • Harder: every name in phantom.api is a promise; a session with dynamics costs about 1 ms per sample (one matrix exponential), so long maps belong in dynamics=False or charge="mean"; a point evaluated alone and inside a batch agree within 1e-12 relative, not bit for bit (numpy's kernels).
  • Must now: the owner tags v0.2.0 after this merges; the qdt side (#140, #141, #142) pins it; the compiled rates are constant at runtime (State says so) until a later step makes them voltage- dependent; the wiring draw's sensor-coupling asymmetry is not yet applied by runtime_sensor.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Device methods only, no phantom.api — rejected: compile_device lives above device, so a consumer would import from three layers and the surface would have no single place to snapshot.
  • sense returns the equilibrium average only — rejected: qdt samples a charge state per shot, and a trace at a degeneracy must switch; the average stays available as charge="mean".
  • A noise seed that redraws the noise parameters — rejected: the amplitudes and switchers are the device's draw (ADR 0019); only the realisation belongs to a run.
  • Sampling the charge per sample from the propagated distribution — rejected: it loses the correlation between consecutive samples that a slow lead produces; the trajectory keeps it.
  • wait(duration_s, v) instead of hold(v, duration_s) — hold names the gate point first like sense, and wait stays the hold at the last point.

docs.title: 0025 — A session tags a release when the owner says so, on a green main with the changelog entry; the owner can always tag
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-27 Step: 8

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR 0024 decided that the owner tags releases, and issue #40's checklist said the same. After PR #44 the owner asked that a session be able to tag when told to (#45), so that a release does not wait on the owner running git. A tag is what consumers pin (qdt pins phantom by tag, ADR 0003), so the tagged commit must be one that CI has passed and whose changelog names the version. Trying it on 2026-10-27, the session's branch pushes succeeded but its push of v0.2.0 was refused with HTTP 403, and its GitHub tools have no call that creates a tag: whether a session can tag depends on the credentials of its environment.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Release bullet of ADR 0024, amended: a session tags a release only when the owner says so in the conversation. The tag is annotated, named vX.Y.Z after pyproject.toml's version, and points at a commit on main whose CI run is green and whose CHANGELOG.md has the X.Y.Z entry. The session confirms all three before tagging and says on the step's issue which commit it tagged.
  • The owner can always tag directly, on GitHub's release page or with git.
  • A session whose environment refuses the tag push says so and leaves the tag to the owner. It never works around the refusal through another channel.
  • How often phantom releases and qdt moves its pin stays the owner's open decision (Step 8).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Easier: a release can be cut in the same conversation that finishes it.
  • Harder: a session has three preconditions to check before a tag, and a tag pushed by mistake has to be deleted by hand on GitHub, where consumers may already have fetched it.
  • Must now: CLAUDE.md carries the rule; the documents that said "the owner tags releases" (CHANGELOG.md, docs/CONTRACT.md, the Step 8 file) say this instead. v0.2.0 itself is tagged by the owner, because this session's environment refused the push.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Keep tagging the owner's alone (ADR 0024 as written): rejected at the owner's request.
  • A CI workflow that tags when the version in pyproject.toml changes on main: rejected for now. It tags without anyone saying so, and the owner wants the decision to release kept explicit.
  • Let a session tag whenever a step closes: rejected, since cadence is the owner's open decision.

docs.title: 0026 — The sensor is a dot with its own barriers and bath: compiled leads, a lifetime-broadened current, its charging energy and coupling from the layout
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-29 Step: 7 (issue #47, after the Step 8 release)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The charge sensor was a potential minimum under one gate (SG) with nothing on either side of it: in the textbook layout the potential rose back to the ungated level, so the sensor had no barriers and no leads, and nothing could tune its coupling. Its Coulomb-peak shape was qdt-sim's typed SET: a peak period of 0.25 V of a "V-equivalent" sensor potential φ_s with a lever arm of 4·10⁻³ eV/V, a thermal energy of 80 µeV, a peak current of 1 nA and a per-electron coupling of −4 and −3 mV. Its peaks were about 1 V apart on SG, a hundred times a real sensor dot's spacing.

The owner asked for barriers and a bath that can be tuned. Giving the typed sensor rates alone does not work: compile moves SG onto the flank of the nearest peak, up to half a period (0.5 V) away, and a sensor dot whose barriers come from the landscape is pinched off or wide open after such a move (rates from 10⁻²⁰ to 10¹² Hz in a scan). Real barriers only make sense on a sensor whose peaks are as far apart as its charging energy says. The closed-form potential has no absolute Fermi level and no screening (ADR 0013), so the absolute energies of a dot and a lead do not say where electrons tunnel; the qubit dots' lead rates use the higher of the dot's ground level and the lead's band bottom plus 2 meV, and are constant at runtime. The noise draw's switcher amplitudes (ADR 0019) are stated in the typed sensor's φ_s units.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Give the textbook layout a sensor channel of the qubit channel's pattern (barrier gates SB_L, SB_R and bath gates SR_L, SR_R), and make a compiled sensor with leads a dot like the qubit dots: its rates compiled from its barriers with their gate slopes and an attempt-rate ceiling, its baths conducting above an accumulation threshold, its current the lifetime-broadened single-level sum, and its charging energy, coupling and temperature from the layout and the device. Specifically:

  • Geometry. The four gates are listed after the first eight, which keep their order; the sensor's search region spans its barriers. A layout without the named sensor reservoirs keeps the typed sensor.
  • Charging energy and coupling. From the three-dot capacitance matrix (the double dot's 2×2 block, the sensor's total capacitance by the qubit dots' rule, sphere mutual capacitances): E_c,s = e²(C⁻¹)_ss and β_i = −(e/1 V)(C⁻¹)_si. φ_s is the potential at the dot in volts (lever arm 1 eV/V), the peak period is E_c,s, the thermal width 2kT at the device temperature, and the wiring draw's asymmetry multiplies β (ADR 0016). The sensor's charge does not act back on the dots.
  • Rates. Each lead's rate is f_attempt·exp(−2S) through its barrier to the centroid of its bath gate, at a tunnelling level placed once by the qubit dots' rule at the wired programmed point and held fixed: on a Coulomb peak electrons tunnel at the leads' electrochemical potential, which no gate moves. The slopes d ln Γ/dV against every gate are central differences of ±10 mV at that level. At runtime the exponent moves with the slopes and a logistic, anchored to give the compiled rate exactly, saturates it at the attempt rate.
  • Baths. A bath conducts with the occupation of a soft step where the electron energy at its gate's centroid (linear in the gate voltages, with the draw's offset) crosses −50 meV over 4 meV, the turn-on protocols' placeholder (calibration none); it multiplies that lead's rate.
  • Current. I = e·Γ_SΓ_D/(Γ_S + Γ_D)·Σ_k [n_γ(μ_k − eV/2) − n_γ(μ_k + eV/2)] with n_γ the Fermi function convolved with a Lorentzian of full width γ = ħ(Γ_S + Γ_D), in closed form through the complex digamma function (readout.broadening, entries beenakker1991-coulomb-blockade and foxman1993-quantum-levels-coulomb-island, both proposed). No typed background: between peaks the current is the Lorentzian tails. Spin degeneracy is not counted.
  • Set point. One step onto the flank and a re-derivation, as before, then one more step with the re-derived sensor and its leads, without deriving again, the peak width taken at the step's own target (three fixed passes). The sensor's linearisation and leads are the ones the set point used; the double dot is derived again at the final point.
  • Noise. The draw's switcher amplitudes are multiplied by the ratio of the sensor dot's mean coupling to the typed sensor's, so a switcher keeps its size against a dot electron's signal.
  • Consumers. State.sensor_gamma_hz; Knowable.sensor_barrier_gates, sensor_reservoir_gates; SensorTruth.lifetime_width_v, gamma_source_hz, gamma_drain_hz, with the wing and slope of the broadened lineshape (the steepest point, by bisection on Re ψ‴); SensorLeads in phantom.api; DEVICE_FORMAT_VERSION 2; release 0.3.0.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Easier: a consumer tunes the sensor as on a device: a bath turn-on, a barrier pinch-off, a barrier–barrier map with a diagonal Coulomb line, peaks tens of mV apart on SG that grow and then broaden towards e²/h as the barriers open; the sensor's charging energy and coupling come from the same geometry as the qubit dots'; the truth states the rates and the broadened wing.
  • Harder: the rates inherit the closed-form potential's sensitivity, a factor e every 3–5 mV on a sensor barrier or SG, and a wide bath gate reaches under the adjacent barrier about as strongly as the barrier gate itself; the runtime exponential stays within 20 % of the compile tier over ±10 mV and drifts beyond (a factor 12 at −30 mV on SG). A sharp, strongly coupled sensor makes raw stability maps look like a real uncompensated sensor's, and the gate 1/f noise now moves it visibly. The common programmed point's sensor barriers are set for seed 2: four of seeds 0–11 form no sensor dot there.
  • Must now: qdt moves its pin to 0.3.0 and adds the four gates; device files from 0.2.0 do not load (recompile from the seed); a consumer tunes SG before reading, since the programmed SG alone usually sits between peaks; screening (plan §8 #1) is what would temper the sensitivity.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Rates on the typed sensor, its peak shape kept — rejected: the set point's half-period move of SG (0.5 V) pinches the barriers or removes them, so the compiled rates are a near-random function of the draw; the typed 80 µeV thermal energy and the device's 13 µeV also disagree.
  • Rates constant at runtime, as the qubit dots' leads — rejected: the request is barriers and a bath that tune; the sensor's rates are what a sensor tune-up moves.
  • The tunnelling level following the dot's ground state at every gate point — rejected: raising SG then closes the sensor and the compile tier and runtime disagree in sign between devices; the level pinned at the leads' electrochemical potential is the physical choice for a many-electron sensor on a peak.
  • Sequential tunnelling without lifetime broadening — rejected: opening the barriers would raise the current without bound, past the conductance quantum.
  • A bath as a series resistance — rejected for now: it needs a 2DEG mobility and a self-consistent bias division; the occupation step uses the threshold the turn-on protocols already use.
  • Iterating the set point with re-derivations to a tolerance — rejected: the sensor potential α·V jumps by several peak widths when a re-derivation moves the dot minimum by a grid step, so it does not converge, and a tolerance test differs between platforms (ADR 0014).

docs.title: 0027 — The qubit dots' rates follow the gates at runtime: compiled slopes of the WKB action at a fixed tunnelling level, capped at the attempt rate
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-30 Step: 8 follow-up (issue #53, after ADR 0026)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Compile computes the double dot's three rates (dot 1 to the left lead, dot 2 to the right lead, and the transfer between the dots) once, at the operating point. Each is the attempt rate times exp(−2S), with S the WKB action (ADR 0017, 0023). At runtime they were constants. State reported the same Γ_L, Γ_R and Γ_m at every gate point, and the master equation used them everywhere. On the reference device they are 10⁹–10¹¹ Hz, so every dwell from a microsecond up saw equilibrium. No barrier gate could slow a lead into the range where latching or telegraph switching shows, although the rate equation and the Markov trajectories that would show them were already built.

ADR 0026 gave the sensor's own leads gate-dependent rates: slopes d ln Γ/dV against every gate at a tunnelling level held fixed, and a logistic that caps the rate at the attempt rate. The owner asked for the same for the qubit dots (2026-10-30: "gates to modulate those dynamics").

The closed-form potential has no screening (#48). On seed 2 the slopes of ln Γ_L reach 213/V on P1, 173/V on R_L and 119/V on B_L. The slope of Γ_m on B_M is 232/V, which equals 2/v_scale of the interdot coupling t. That is expected: t ∝ √T and Γ_m ∝ T come from the same cut.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The dots' lead and interdot rates follow the gates at runtime. The rule is the one ADR 0026 set for the sensor's leads:

  • Compile places each barrier's tunnelling level once at the operating point, by tunnelling_level_ev, and holds it fixed.
  • It then takes the central differences (±10 mV) of the action against every gate at that level.
  • At runtime the exponent moves linearly with those slopes, and saturating_rates_hz, shared with the sensor's leads, anchors the rate at the compiled one and caps it at the dot's attempt rate.

Specifically:

  • Record. CompiledBarrier gains attempt_rate_hz, tunnelling_level_ev and log_rate_slopes_per_v. The compiled rates are unchanged bit for bit. DEVICE_FORMAT_VERSION 3.
  • Runtime. readout.rates.GateRates holds the reference point, the rates, the attempt rates and the slopes. RateEquation.gate_rates is optional: when it is given, each rate matrix takes its three rates at its own voltages, and without it the rates are the constants as before. Device.runtime_rates() always gives it.
  • Consumer surface. State.gamma_left_hz, gamma_right_hz and gamma_interdot_hz are arrays with the input's leading axes, at the carried voltages. Truth keeps the compiled values at the operating point. A session's dynamics use the rates at each sample's voltages, gate noise included.
  • Equilibrium. Only the prefactors move, so detailed balance and the Boltzmann stationary state are exact at every point (P0).
  • Release. This is folded into the untagged 0.3.0, as the owner decided. Model versions: compile.device 4, device 4, device.session 3.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Easier:
  • A consumer closes B_L or B_R and slows the lead into the kilohertz range. On seed 2, Γ_L at dot 1's transition is about 10⁴ Hz with B_L 0.1 V lower.
  • A sweep there latches. At 3 µs per point the transition opens into a loop about 3 mV wide.
  • A parked sampled session telegraphs from the dot's own lead, and closing B_M slows interdot transfer.
  • The gallery shows all of this (session-closing-barrier).
  • Harder:
  • The rates inherit the unscreened sensitivity: a factor e every 4–10 mV, P1 moves Γ_L more than B_L does, and a reservoir gate reaches the lead barrier strongly (#48).
  • Across one P1 transition Γ_L changes by about e⁸. Within ±10 mV the runtime exponent stays within 20 % of the action's change plus the grid's step (about 0.1 in ln Γ). Beyond that the linear exponent drifts from the compile tier.
  • The equilibrium stays exact, but the time scales far from the operating point are an extrapolation.
  • Must now:
  • State's three rates are arrays. A consumer that cached a scalar rate reads it per point.
  • Device files from earlier 0.3.0 commits do not load; recompile them from their seed.
  • The contract's hold check settles for the slower of its two points.
  • session-hold-relaxation overlays the total rate out of the held state at the read point. Its earlier overlay, exp(−Γ_L t), left out the interdot path that empties through dot 2's lead. That path made the mean relax twice as fast on the gallery device before this change too.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• The tunnelling level following the dot's ground state at each point. Rejected for the same reason as in ADR 0026. At a charge transition the electron tunnels at the leads' electrochemical potential, which no gate moves. With a moving level, a plunger would close its own dot's lead instead of opening it, and the compile tier and the runtime would disagree.
  • Only the barrier gate's own slope (B_L on Γ_L, and so on), like t's single-gate Barrier. Rejected: the action responds to every gate, the plunger more strongly than the barrier in this potential. Dropping that would make the rates follow a gate the potential barely weights.
  • Recomputing the action at runtime. Rejected by ADR 0001: a line cut through the basis per sample is far slower than 1 ms per point.
  • The rates as an exponential without a ceiling. Rejected: opening a barrier would raise the rate past the attempt frequency.
  • A new release, 0.4.0, for this change. Rejected by the owner: 0.3.0 is untagged and nobody pins it, so one breaking release carries the sensor dot and the dots' dynamics.

docs.title: 0028 — The sensor dot's charge is a process in time: a birth–death chain over its levels on the session clock, counted electrons per dwell, and back-action on the dots against its mean
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-30 Step: 8 follow-up (issue #54, after ADR 0026 and 0027)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
After ADR 0026 the sensor is a dot with barriers and baths. Its rates follow its gates. Its current, though, was the stationary current at each sample's voltages and dot charge, so only the two qubit dots' charge evolved in a session.

A real sensor with a barrier nearly pinched off does not give a smooth small current. Its own occupation switches, the current arrives one electron at a time, and a slow sensor reads late or misses a transition. The owner asked for this, with the gates setting the regime. They also chose to include back-action, always on with dynamics: the sensor's charge shifts the dots' levels through the mutual capacitance by which the dots shift the sensor.

Three forces shaped the design:

  • Cost. A session pays one matrix exponential over the dots' 25-state window per sample (about 0.2–0.6 ms). A joint chain over dots × sensor, or exact counting statistics by a counting field, would cost tens of times more.
  • Rates. The sensor's rates span 10⁻⁵ to 10¹¹ Hz with the gates. No single algorithm samples both ends cheaply.
  • Coupling. The coupling is strong: |β| ≈ 0.35 meV ≫ kT = 13 µeV, so a sensor electron moves a dot level by tens of kT.
  • Absolute charges. The closed-form model counts the dots' charge absolutely (about 25 electrons each). A back-action measured from an absolute reference shifts the dots by millivolts. Seed 7 put the sensor 3 electrons below the charge the gates alone induce, a shift of 1.5 meV.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
With dynamics, the sensor dot's charge M is a birth–death chain over its levels on the session clock. Each sample's current is the charge that leaves to the drain during the dwell, divided by the dwell. The sensor acts back on the dots through −β_i·(M − M̄), where M̄ is the mean of its stationary state at the present voltages and dot charge. Specifically:

  • Chain. From M the sensor gains an electron at Γ_S n_S(μ_M) + Γ_D n_D(μ_M) and loses one at Γ_S(1 − n_S(μ_{M−1})) + Γ_D(1 − n_D(μ_{M−1})), with μ_M = E_c(M − x). The leads' occupations are convolved with the level's Lorentzian (readout.broadening). Through one level the stationary current is exactly ADR 0026's. The chain holds both sides of every level within the bias window plus 20 kT, at least both sides of the nearest level, and every charge it still carries. The other levels add their ADR 0026 current as a constant.
  • Counted charge.
  • When the chain makes at most 200 jumps in a dwell, the counted charge and the end state come from an exact trajectory.
  • Otherwise the count is Gaussian. Its mean, given the start state, comes from one augmented matrix exponential. Its variance is the long-time variance of full counting statistics (1ᵀJ₂p − 2·1ᵀJ₁W^D J₁p), and the end state is drawn from e^{WT}.
  • In mean mode the distribution is propagated and the expected count is read.
  • Once the dwell spans more than 50 of the chain's relaxation times, the end state is the stationary p and the integral of e^{Ws}q is T·p + W^D(p − q), in closed form.
  • Order within a sample. The dots step first, with the back-action of the sensor's charge at the start of the dwell. The sensor then steps at the dots' new charge and the sample's switcher shift. A hold evolves both, at the last bias given.
  • Back-action. The shift is −β_i·(M − M̄) per electron on dot i, with the β the sensor reads (wiring asymmetry included). The closed-form potential has no electrons and stands for the sensor at its mean. What it leaves out, and what acts back, is the sensor's switching and its lag. Within a dwell the dots' rates keep detailed balance in the shifted energies.
  • Surface.
  • Measurement.sensor_charge: the sensor's charge at the end of each dwell, or None without dynamics or for a typed sensor.
  • RateEquation.rate_matrix(..., level_shift_ev).
  • The new module readout.sensor_dynamics, with its own random stream [seed, 8, …, 2].
  • Without dynamics, or with a typed sensor, the output is unchanged. device.session MODEL_VERSION 4. Release 0.3.0.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Easier:
  • A consumer closes the sensor's barriers, or lowers a bath gate towards its turn-on, and reads single-electron bursts and the sensor's own telegraph.
  • A slow sensor misses a dot transition that a fast one reads cleanly (session-slow-sensor).
  • The shot noise of a fast sensor shrinks as 1/√dwell, with the Fano factor of the chain.
  • A sensor that lags or switches shifts the dots by its coupling.
  • Harder:
  • The splitting is first order in the dwell. Within one dwell the sensor sees the dots' charge at its end, and the dots see the sensor's charge at its start. A dot jump therefore reaches the sensor's rates in the sample where it happens, and the sensor's lag, not a sample's delay, is what makes a slow sensor late.
  • Putting the broadened occupations into sequential rates is phenomenological. It is exact in its stationary mean and in the thermal limit, but its noise is the sequential one.
  • The chain has no joint energy with the dots: detailed balance holds per step, not over the joint process.
  • At ΓT ≈ 10⁸ the augmented exponential keeps only about eight digits, and they differ between platforms. The first Windows comparison differed by 1.5·10⁻⁹. Beyond 50 relaxation times, propagate therefore uses the relaxed closed form T·p + W^D(p − q) (ADR 0014).
  • A session with a sensor with leads costs about 0.3–0.7 ms per sample, against 0.2.
  • Must now: a consumer that reads n_present alone still gets the dots. sensor_charge counts on the level numbering of φ_s, so only its changes are physical.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• A joint chain over dots × sensor states. Rejected for cost: about 50–75 states and a matrix exponential per sample, plus counting fields for the current.
  • A back-action reference at the induced charge (x₀ + ½, or x(N) + ½). Rejected: with the model's absolute dot charge it shifts the dots by millivolts (seed 7: 1.5 meV) or adds a (β·N)² term.
  • Exact trajectories at every rate. Rejected: a fast sensor makes 10⁸ jumps in a millisecond.
  • The Gaussian count at every rate. Rejected: it cannot show single-electron bursts.
  • Back-action off, or opt-in. Rejected by the owner, who chose it always on with dynamics.
  • A sample's current as the instantaneous stationary current of the sensor's state. Rejected: it shows neither bursts nor shot noise, and its long-dwell mean is not the counted charge.

docs.title: 0029 — The interdot coupling follows the gates and hybridizes the charge states: t from half the slopes of ln Γ_m, capped at ħω₀/π; eigenstates of the CI window in the statics and a Pauli master equation over them in the dynamics
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-31 Step: 8 follow-up (issue #58, the first of #58–#60; after ADR 0027)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
In a simulated tune-up the owner found that "the barrier gates do not actually modulate the interdot coupling AT ALL" (2026-10-31). On 0.3.0:

  • t on paper only. State.tunnel_coupling_ev was t₀·exp((V_BM − V₀)/v_scale): it followed the barrier gate alone, had no ceiling (15 meV at B_M + 50 mV on the reference device) and entered nothing a sensor reads. It reached only the exchange and the transport placeholders.
  • A classical charge. The sensor read the classical CI model and its rate equation. Opening B_M did not change an interdot line, apart from the interdot rate of ADR 0027 and a fixed cross-capacitance.
  • The owner's decisions (2026-10-31). Hybridize the charge states in the statics and the dynamics. Reshape the dots with a compiled grid in #59. Follow with the exchange in #60. Release all three as 0.4.0.

Four forces shaped the design:

  • Cost. State is evaluated on grids of 10⁴–10⁵ points, and a session pays one matrix exponential per sample. A per-point diagonalisation must stay at microseconds.
  • Consistency. ADR 0027 already compiles the slopes of ln Γ_m against every gate at a fixed tunnelling level. Γ_m ∝ T and t ∝ √T come from the same cut.
  • Limits. At t → 0 the result must be the CI model, which the P0 tests and every earlier protocol rely on.
  • Reproducibility (ADR 0014). Eigenvalues near 0.05 eV with kT = 13 µeV lose digits in a Boltzmann weight unless the matrix is conditioned.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The interdot coupling follows every gate, and the CI window's charge states of one total charge hybridize through it. The statics use the window's eigenstates, and the dynamics are a Pauli master equation over them. Specifically:

  • t at the gates. t(V) = t_max·σ(ln(t_ref/(t_max − t_ref)) + ½ s_m·ΔV):
  • t_ref is the compiled t at the operating point.
  • s_m are the slopes of ln Γ_m of ADR 0027.
  • t_max = ħω₀/π is compile's t = ħω₀√T/π at a transmission of one.
  • The form is saturating_rates_hz's. charge.hybrid.InterdotCoupling carries it, and Device.runtime_coupling() builds it from fields the device file already has, so the device format is unchanged.
  • Hybridization.
  • H_N = Σ U(N)|N⟩⟨N| − t Σ(|N₁+1, N₂−1⟩⟨N₁, N₂| + h.c.) on the window's states of each total charge, spinless with one level per dot.
  • The window is the CI window's (2w+1)² grid with its centre held at or above zero, and a negative occupation left out.
  • Each block is a chain of at most 2w+1 states, diagonalised in batches with its lowest level taken out first, so the eigenvalues keep their digits.
  • Charges are summed relative to the window's centre.
  • Statics. With a coupling, ConstantInteractionParams gives the occupation as the diagonal of the thermal density matrix of the eigenstates. ⟨N⟩, the sensor's potential and current, and the lock-in follow from it. The ground state is the dominant charge state of the lowest eigenstate. Without a coupling the model is unchanged, bit for bit.
  • Dynamics. RateEquation.eigen_rate_matrix gives the rates between eigenstates:
  • Lead i adds an electron from k to l at Γ_i·|⟨l|c†_i|k⟩|²·f((E_l − E_k)/kT) and removes it at the complement.
  • Within a total charge, k relaxes to l at Γ_m·g_kl·f(·), with g_kl = Σ_b w_bk·w_bl the product of the two eigenstates' weights on each bond b between charge states one moved electron apart. That is the sum of |⟨l|X_b|k⟩|² + |⟨l|Z_b|k⟩|², the bond's transfer and its dipole.
  • g is exactly Γ_m's classical rule at t = 0, and Γ_m for an isolated pair at every detuning.
  • Detailed balance holds in the eigenenergies.
  • When the gates move, the distribution is projected onto the new eigenstates, q_l = Σ_k p_k|⟨l|k⟩|², with coherences dropped. sweep and Session share this.
  • What a sample reads. A sampled session draws an eigenstate, and the sensor reads its ⟨N⟩. Its total charge is an integer and its split need not be. Measurement.n_present is that charge, and the contract checks the total. State.tunnel_coupling_ev is the gated t.
  • Release. 0.4.0 (breaking). Model versions: charge.hybrid 1, readout.master_equation 2, device 5, device.session 5, optimum.targets 2.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Easier:
  • Opening B_M widens an interdot line from the thermal step to ½(1 − ε/Ω·tanh(Ω/2kT)). On the reference device the 10–90 % width goes from 0.22 mV to 0.65 mV as t goes from 0.05 to 30 µeV (interdot-line-vs-barrier).
  • Closing B_M is what isolates a dot. With B_L closed alone, dot 2's lead loads dot 1 at Γ_R·t²(1/Δ + 1/Δ')². The electron-like and hole-like paths add, as in elastic cotunnelling, at about 10⁶ Hz against Γ_L ≈ 10⁴ Hz. With both closed, a sweep latches and a parked point telegraphs (session-closing-barrier).
  • optimum(device).coupling inverts the same t a session uses.
  • Harder:
  • Validity of the projection. The projection assumes a dwell long against ħ/Ω and dephasing in the eigenbasis. At |ε| ≲ t it shares the electron between the dots even when t is so small that the coherent transfer would take longer than the dwell (t ≲ ħ/dwell, sub-neV at microsecond dwells). On the reference device t stays above 0.05 µeV, and a sweep lands that close to a degeneracy rarely. There is no charge-dephasing rate and no Landau–Zener step.
  • Plunger sensitivity. t inherits the unscreened sensitivity of #48. The plungers move it as much as B_M, and two cells 18 mV apart on B_M differ by a factor of 30 in t at their interdot lines.
  • Fixed shape and spin. The dots' capacitances, lever arms and positions stay those of the operating point until #59. The model is spinless, so there is no √2 on singlet tunnelling (that is #60's sector) and no valley structure.
  • Cost. A grid point costs about 7 µs instead of 1.3 µs in the statics, and a sample a few small diagonalisations more.
  • Exchange. J still comes from the Hubbard model with the barrier-only exponential, so State.exchange_ev and State.tunnel_coupling_ev disagree until #60.
  • Must now:
  • A consumer that labels charge states from n_present rounds it. An interdot line is no longer a step.
  • A test that isolates a dot closes its own barrier and B_M.
  • The contract's sample_semantics and hold_moves_the_charge checks compare the total charge.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Hybridizing statics only. Rejected by the owner. A session's charge would disagree with State near every interdot line.
  • A separate slope compile for t (central differences of interdot_tunnel_coupling_ev per gate). Rejected. It costs 24 more barrier actions per compile, its level moves with the gates (the rule ADR 0027 rejected), and ADR 0027 already shows the two agree on B_M.
  • Full density-matrix (Bloch–Redfield) dynamics. Rejected for cost: 25² states per sample. A charge-dephasing rate and a Landau–Zener step would lift the projection's limit, and are left for when a protocol needs them.
  • Incoherent resonant tunnelling between localized states (a Lorentzian Γ(ε)). Rejected. It cannot give the polarization width √(ε² + 4t²) at t ≫ kT, which is what a tune-up reads.
  • One 25×25 diagonalisation per point. Rejected. Different total charges are degenerate across blocks, so the eigenvectors could mix them, and it costs more.
  • An integer n_present (the eigenstate's dominant charge state) beside a non-integer sensor input. Rejected: n_present would no longer be what entered the sensor.

docs.title: 0030 — The barrier gates reshape the dots through a compiled grid: the double dot re-derived along each barrier gate, its changes interpolated and added at runtime, held where the dots merge
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-31 Step: 8 follow-up (issue #59, the second of #58–#60; after ADR 0029)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
After ADR 0029 the interdot coupling followed the gates, but the dots themselves did not. Compile placed them once at the operating point. Their positions, sizes, lever arms, the disorder offsets at them, the capacitance matrix and the actions of the barriers around them then held at every gate point. A barrier gate only moved the dots' levels through a fixed cross-capacitance, and through the linear slopes of the rates and of t. The owner asked for the barrier gates to change the dots' "potential locations/shape" (2026-10-31), and decided on a grid compiled along the barrier gates and interpolated at runtime.

Five forces shaped the design:

  • Compile once, run cheap (ADR 0001). A derivation of the double dot costs 1.5 ms plus three barrier actions, so a runtime point cannot call one. A grid of 17 nodes per gate costs about 0.2 s of compile.
  • A nonlinear potential map. The closed-form potential is linear in the gates, but the minimum is not. On the reference device, B_M at +0.15 V draws the dots 18 nm together, C_m grows by 40 % and dot 1's addition energy falls by 1 meV. At +0.18 V the potential forms one dot. B_L and B_R move their own dot by several nm and merge it with its lead when opened far enough.
  • Pixel steps. find_dots places a minimum on a 2 nm grid point. Taken directly, positions and lever arms jump in steps.
  • Bit-exact anchor. At the operating point nothing may change: the compiled device and every test there stay exact.
  • File size. The device file must stay small, and the basis is not stored.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Compile re-derives the double dot along each barrier gate and records each quantity's change from the operating point. The runtime interpolates each gate's changes and adds them. Specifically:

  • The grid.
  • CompileParams.shape_gates (B_L, B_M, B_R), shape_span_v (±0.2 V) and shape_points (17).
  • At each node only that gate moves.
  • Each dot's minimum is refined between grid points by a parabola (refined_dot). Its lever arms and disorder offset are taken there.
  • The capacitance matrix is the derivation's own formula (capacitance_matrix_af) at the refined dots.
  • The three barrier actions are taken at the tunnelling levels held fixed (ADR 0027), from the refined dots.
  • Each grid runs outward from the operating point until the potential stops forming two dots, or a dot jumps by more than 12 nm. In that case it merged and another minimum took its place, and the end is marked merged.
  • charge.shape.ShapeGrid holds the nodes and the changes. Device.shape, DEVICE_FORMAT_VERSION 4.
  • The runtime.
  • Each gate's changes are interpolated with PCHIP at its carried voltage and the gates' changes are added.
  • Beyond a grid's end the changes are held. ShapeGrid.merged flags a point beyond a merged end.
  • ConstantInteractionParams.shape gives C(V) and n_g = C(V)·(α(V)·V − Δo(V))/E_UNIT. This is the potential at the moved minimum, by the envelope theorem, and it is exact to first order in the plungers, which stay linear.
  • InterdotCoupling.shape and GateRates.shape take the exponents along the barrier gates from the grid (t from half the interdot change). The compiled slopes still serve every other gate.
  • The consumer surface. State gains dot_positions_nm, dot_radii_nm, addition_energies_ev and dots_merged. optimum(device).coupling inverts t along the barrier gate by Brent's method.
  • The hybridized window (amends ADR 0029).
  • The window centres on rint(n_g), which changes at the middle of every interdot segment (n_g = N + ½), the very point a tune-up reads. With t near a meV the ±2 chains of ADR 0029 left a seam of 2·10⁻⁵ e there. The first Windows comparison of this change differed by 1.8·10⁻⁵ when last-digit rounding put a point on the other side.
  • The statics now use a ±4 window. Its truncation, about (t/E_add)^(2w), stays below 10⁻¹² up to t's ceiling, at about 25 µs per point instead of 7.
  • The dynamics use the smallest window whose truncation is below 10⁻¹³ at each sample's t (dynamics_window): ±2 below t/E_add = 10⁻³, ±3 below 1.5·10⁻², ±4 above.
  • charge.hybrid 2, readout.master_equation 3.
  • The session's propagator (ADR 0014).
  • With the dots shaped, a latching sweep reads its slow transition through entries of exp(W·dt) that sit beside rates 10⁵ times faster. A general exponential keeps its error near ε‖W·dt‖ in absolute terms. Over a hundred latched steps and the sensor's flank, session-closing-barrier differed by 1.1·10⁻⁹ on Windows and 5·10⁻⁹ on macOS.
  • readout.master_equation.propagator computes exp(W·dt) with every entry accurate relative to itself. It takes the Taylor series of the non-negative W + aI over a step with a·h ≤ ½, then squares a non-negative matrix, putting each column back to one. 10⁻¹⁶ relative noise in it now moves the protocol by 7·10⁻¹³.
  • Session uses it. The Step 4 sweeps and the sensor's chain keep expm.
  • Release. 0.4.0. Model versions: charge.shape 1, compile.device 5, device 6, device.session 6, optimum.targets 3.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Easier:
  • A barrier gate moves its dots, changes their size and their addition energies, couples them more strongly and reshapes the honeycomb (dot-shape-vs-barrier).
  • Opening B_M ends in a flagged merge instead of an unbounded extrapolation.
  • The rates and t follow the moved dots. When a barrier falls below its tunnelling level, its action is zero and the rate levels off at f_a/(2 − T₀), about half the attempt rate. Other gates' linear slopes still take it towards f_a.
  • Harder:
  • Separable changes. The gates' changes are added, so cross terms (B_L with B_M on dot 1) are left out. Opening all three barriers together pushes the rates towards the attempt rate.
  • The model's own limits. The capacitances still come from the disk and sphere formulae of ADR
    1. C_m grows only to about 2.1 aF before the merge, so a merged double dot does not become one dot in the CI model. Points beyond the merge hold the last two-dot shape and are flagged.
  • Pixel noise. The compile tier takes a dot's curvature at a grid point, so the radius and the capacitances move in steps of about 1 % as the minimum changes pixel. The interpolant runs through them, and halfway between nodes it is within 2 % of a direct derivation.
  • Absolute charge. The CI model counts the charge absolutely (n_g = Cφ/E ≈ 23 e). A dot that grows by 10 % takes about two more electrons at the same potential, so a barrier gate moves the lines along the plungers by more than its cross-capacitance. Tests and protocols that follow one transition name its electron count.
  • Cost and size. Compile takes 0.2 s more. The device file grows from 14 kB to 62 kB. A State point costs about 25 µs, and a session sample a few interpolations more.
  • Exponent between nodes. An exponent that saturates within one 25 mV step is interpolated coarsely there, by up to 1 in ln Γ.
  • Not yet shaped. The sensor's coupling to the dots (β) and the attempt rates stay at the operating point.
  • Must now:
  • Device files from 0.3.0 and from earlier 0.4.0 commits do not load (format 4); recompile them from their seed.
  • A consumer that cached C_dot, the lever arms or t from the compiled device reads them per point.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• A tensor-product grid over the three barrier gates. Rejected for size and compile time: 17³ derivations and several MB. The cross terms it would capture are second order on the reference device.
  • Linear slopes of each quantity (first derivatives). Rejected by the owner. They cannot show the merge or the saturation, and they drift within tens of mV.
  • Grid-point minima without refinement. Rejected: positions and lever arms would step by 2 nm and the honeycomb would jump.
  • Including the plungers in the grid. Deferred. Their lever arms are the largest, but at the operating point they move the minima less than the barriers do, and the envelope theorem keeps the energies right to first order.
  • Crossing into a single-dot model past the merge. Deferred to the solver (plan §8 #1). The CI model has no state for one dot of N₁ + N₂ electrons. Flagging the merge and holding the last two-dot shape keeps the model honest about what it does not describe.

docs.title: 0031 — The exchange of the dots' valence electrons follows the gates: the singlet secular equation on the CI window's local sector at the gated coupling and the shaped dots; the Pauli readout at the gated coupling
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-31 Step: 8 follow-up (issue #60, the last of #58–#60; after ADR 0029 and 0030)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
After ADR 0029 and 0030 the barrier gates set the interdot coupling and the dots' shape, but not the exchange. State.exchange_ev came from the two-site Hubbard model (ADR 0021). That model holds 0–2 electrons per dot and took t from the barrier gate alone, with no ceiling. A compiled device's dots hold about 23 electrons each, so away from the Hubbard model's own symmetric point J described an unrelated charge configuration. At the reference device's programmed point it read about 13 meV, whether t was 0.14 or 45 µeV. The Pauli spin blockade (PSB) readout used the compiled t, not the t at the gates. The bisection behind J also divided zero by zero where t underflowed: a RuntimeWarning, with a finite J.

The owner asked for the barrier gate to set the exchange frequency (2026-10-31).

Three forces shaped the design:

  • Precision. J spans twelve decades. The secular equation solved relative to E(1,1) keeps its relative digits (ADR 0021), and the charge gaps have to keep theirs.
  • Consistency. The CI window already carries the gated t (ADR 0029) and the shaped capacitances (ADR 0030).
  • Scope. The spin layer's protocols and the coherence optimum use typed or few-electron Hubbard models at their symmetric point, which sits far from the operating point. There, a t extrapolated from the operating point's slopes would mean nothing.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
J at a gate point is the singlet–triplet splitting of the dots' valence electrons, from the two-electron secular equation on the CI window's local sector. Specifically:

  • The sector. The reference is the ground charge state (N₁, N₂) of the hybridized window. The partners are (N₁+1, N₂−1), Δ_L above, and (N₁−1, N₂+1), Δ_R above, at the CI energies at the gates.
  • Each gap is formed directly from N − n_g, as E(δᵀC⁻¹(N − n_g) + ½δᵀC⁻¹δ) with C = C(V), so it keeps its digits.
  • A partner with a negative occupation is left out (Δ = +inf).
  • t is the gated coupling.
  • spin.exchange.local_exchange_ev; the secular solver is shared (singlet_exchange_ev). Where t = 0 it returns J = −min(0, Δ_R, Δ_L) without dividing zero by zero.
  • Meaning. This is the exchange of a qubit pair where both dots hold an odd number of electrons: the effective (1,1). Elsewhere the valence spins are paired, J describes no qubit, and it stays finite. Like the Hubbard model, the sector has spinless orbitals and one valley.
  • The consumer surface.
  • State.exchange_ev is this J, and State.exchange_frequency_hz = J/h.
  • Session.spin_readout reads at the interdot coupling of the last point the session was given.
  • The few-electron Hubbard models, runtime_hubbard and the coherence optimum keep the barrier-gate exponential at their symmetric point.
  • Release. 0.4.0. Model versions: spin.exchange 3, device.session 7.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Easier:
  • The barrier gate sets the exchange frequency. On the reference device's (23, 28) cell, J/h goes from about 1 kHz with B_M 50 mV below the programmed point to 230 MHz at it and to tens of GHz as B_M opens. It follows 2t²(1/Δ_R + 1/Δ_L) while t ≪ Δ and falls below it as t nears the gaps.
  • Across an odd–odd cell, J rises toward both anticrossings (exchange-frequency-vs-barrier).
  • The readout's contrast closes with the barrier.
  • Harder:
  • Jumps. J jumps where the ground charge state changes, because its reference sector changes with it. Inside a cell it is smooth.
  • No spin structure. There are no valleys or orbital excitations in the sector, so for multi-electron valence shells J is the single-orbital estimate.
  • Two exchanges. The Hubbard models in the spin layer still give the few-electron J of ADR 0021 at their symmetric point, so a device's State.exchange_ev and optimum(device).coherence describe different charge configurations.
  • Implausibly large J. t inherits the unscreened sensitivity of #48, so J reaches tens of GHz within tens of mV.
  • Must now:
  • A consumer reads J and J/h per point.
  • A consumer reads the effective (1,1) from the parity of n_ground.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Hubbard models placed at the device's valence electrons per point. Rejected: a 16×16 diagonalisation per point, the same physics as the secular equation, and it loses J's digits (ADR 0021).
  • J as NaN outside odd–odd cells. Rejected: the contract requires State to be finite. The parity is available from n_ground.
  • The spin layer's sweet spot and gate fidelity on the device's local sector. Deferred. It would move the coherence optimum to the operating point's cell, a change to a signed-off-class protocol family, and should be its own issue.
  • The compiled t in the readout. Rejected: the owner asked for the readout to follow the barrier gates too.

docs.title: 0032 — The interdot conductance sets the triple-point splitting: Kemble's transmission of the interdot barrier, Golden & Halperin's f(g), an effective interdot capacitance in the CI model
docs.text: Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-31 Step: 8 follow-up (issue #66; after ADR 0029–0031)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
After #58–#60 the owner still did not see the behaviour they were tuning for: "if I increase the barrier gate between plunger gates, the interdot width (in anti-detuning) should get bigger until I form a superdot underneath the barrier gate. The opposite should also be true, a lower barrier gate voltage should shrink the interdot width until all I see is a grid" (2026-10-31). That width is the triple points' separation. On the reference device, the fractional splitting f = 2C_m/(C_t + C_m) moved only from 0.14 to 0.16 over ±0.2 V of B_M:

  • Geometry. C_m came from the sphere formula of ADR 0013, which B_M changed by about 0.7 aF.
  • Hybridization. ADR 0029's coupling rounds the interdot line but shifts the triple points by at most 2t/E_add ≈ 0.15.
  • No superdot. A single tunnelling level cannot produce the merged dot at all.

In double-dot transport the splitting follows the interdot conductance through quantum charge fluctuations (Waugh et al. 1995; review: van der Wiel et al. 2003, the honeycomb from a grid to one dot). Golden & Halperin give f(g) for N_ch channels of conductance g each, with a weak and a strong limit that do not interpolate reliably for N_ch = 2.

The owner chose (2026-10-31): - a conductance-driven splitting entering the CI model as an effective interdot capacitance; - a smooth interpolation between the published limits; - folding it into 0.4.0.

Four forces shaped the design:

  • Continuity to the merge. The conductance has to reach 1 continuously as the dots merge. WKB's e^(−2S) stops at S = 0, and the rates' logistic halves it.
  • Bit-exact limit. Without conductance nothing may change.
  • Gate charge. The tunnelling relaxes charge quantization. It must not move the gates' induced charge.
  • References. Every published curve enters as a proposed reference entry (ADR 0007).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The interdot conductance per channel is Kemble's transmission of the interdot barrier, and Golden & Halperin's f(g) sets an effective interdot capacitance in the CI model. Specifically:

  • The barrier.
  • Compile records the top ΔU of the interdot barrier above its fixed tunnelling level (ADR 0027), negative below it: the highest U on the straight cut between the dots, sampled bilinearly.
  • It also records ΔU's slopes against every gate, with the dots held, and its curvature ħω_b (a parabola fitted ±4 nm around the top). The shape grid gains a barrier_top_ev column, the top with the dots moved.
  • Device fields interdot_barrier_top_ev, interdot_barrier_top_slopes_ev_per_v and interdot_barrier_hbar_omega_ev; DEVICE_FORMAT_VERSION 5.
  • The conductance. g = 1/(1 + exp(2πΔU/ħω_b)) (Kemble), with N_ch = 2 (spin). It is ½ when the level reaches the top, and it goes continuously towards 1 as the barrier sinks to the merge.
  • The splitting.
  • f_GH(g) joins (2 ln 2/π²)·N_ch·g (g ≤ 0.15) and 1 + (16e^γ/π³)(1 − g)·ln(1 − g) (g ≥ 0.85) with a monotone cubic (calibration: none).
  • The total is f = f_C + (F_max − f_C)·f_GH(g), with f_C = 2C_m/(C_t + C_m) of the geometric capacitances and F_max = 0.98.
  • The CI model.
  • ConstantInteractionParams.splitting adds ΔC_m·[[1, −1], [−1, 1]] to the capacitances in the energies, with ΔC_m = (F_max − f_C)·f_GH·(C_t + C_m)/(2(1 − f)). That is exactly zero at g = 0.
  • The gate-induced charge keeps the geometric capacitances.
  • The CI model's measured splitting along the symmetric axis is f (P0).
  • The consumer surface. State.interdot_conductance and State.interdot_splitting; Device.runtime_splitting().
  • References. golden1996-peak-splitting, waugh1995-tunable-coupling and kemble1935-wkb-barrier as proposed entries, and the honeycomb evolution as an item of vanderwiel2003-double-dot-transport.
  • Release. 0.4.0. Model versions: charge.splitting 1, charge.shape 2, compile.device 6, device 7, device.session 8.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Easier:
  • Opening B_M takes the honeycomb from small hexagons, through elongated hexagons, to the diagonal lines of one superdot, and closing it shrinks the segments back (honeycomb-vs-barrier).
  • On the reference device g rises from 0.002 at the operating point to 0.99 at B_M +50 mV, and f from 0.16 to 0.94. Where the dots merge, f holds at 0.98.
  • The exchange (ADR 0031) and every other CI quantity see the same capacitances.
  • Harder:
  • No exact grid. Closing B_M shrinks f only to the geometric f_C ≈ 0.14. The sphere-formula C_m has no screening by the barrier gate (#48), so the "grid" is small hexagons, not a grid.
  • Steep rise. f rises within about 40 mV of B_M. Kemble's transmission changes by e for every ħω_b/2π ≈ 0.7 meV of barrier height, and the unscreened barrier moves fast with the gates (#48).
  • The f(g) curve. Between g = 0.15 and 0.85 it is an interpolation, which the authors themselves call unreliable for N_ch = 2. A digitised measurement (Waugh et al.) would replace it as a P1 row.
  • Mixed models. The splitting is the metallic-dot theory (many levels) applied to semiconductor dots of about 23 electrons. It sits on top of ADR 0029's single-level hybridization, and the two overlap by at most 2t/E_add.
  • Asymmetry. For unequal dots f uses the mean total capacitance (the symmetric-equivalent definition).
  • Must now:
  • Device files from earlier 0.4.0 commits do not load (format 5).
  • A test that checks the shape's own capacitances turns the splitting off.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• A better electrostatic C_m from the potential (overlapping charge densities). Rejected by the owner. It is closer to the geometry, but it cannot reach the superdot without a solver, and it moves f little.
  • Fitting measured f(g) (Waugh, Livermore) now. Deferred. The curve has to be digitised and confirmed by a human before it can be the standard (ADR 0007).
  • The WKB transmission e^(−2S), or the rates' logistic, as the conductance. Rejected. Either stops at a half (or at one, abruptly) when the barrier falls below the level, so f would jump at the merge.
  • Raising t's ceiling, or several levels per dot. Rejected. The single-level splitting is 2t, and the merged dot needs the many-level charge-fluctuation physics that f(g) summarises.
  • Moving the induced charge with the effective capacitance. Rejected. Tunnelling relaxes charge quantization and does not change how much charge the gates induce.

docs.title: Defect and material catalog
docs.text:
The knowledge only an experienced tuner has: which defects and material traits exist, what they perturb, and what they look like during tune-up. Data, not code (ADR 0006). Schema: SCHEMA.md. Entries: entries/*.yaml. One example entry is provided as a draft with every value marked TODO; the rest are filed as GitHub issues by scripts/issues_catalog.py for a human to write.

Suggested entries (the issue set): interface fixed charge · oxide traps and two-level fluctuators · gate misalignment and width error · gate-to-gate overlap and leakage · open or shorted gate · Ge-concentration fluctuation (valley) · interface steps and roughness · strain variation · residual dopants · dielectric thickness variation · 2DEG density and mobility by material class · sensor-dot coupling asymmetry · charge drift (slow) · material classes SiGe vs MOS as summary traits · (later) Ge holes.

docs.title: Gallery (ADR 0008, 0009)
docs.text:
A stratified set of measurement protocols: sweeps a device of this class is put through, described as physics (gates, ranges, resolution, readout channel, time base, seed). CI renders every protocol on every PR; nothing rendered is stored in git. A human signs each protocol off; a step is settled only when all protocols its layers touch are signed.

View it. On a pull request: the preview link in the sticky comment on the PR, which points at https://cowboyquantum.github.io/phantom/pr-<n>/gallery/rendered/index.html (ADR 0012); it updates a minute or two after each push and is removed when the PR closes. On main: the docs site, "Gallery" in the nav, then the rendered gallery. The CI artifact gallery-ubuntu-latest holds the same files. Locally:

uv run python scripts/gallery.py          # renders to build/gallery/ (gitignored)
uv run mkdocs serve                       # browse it

docs.title: Reference library (ADR 0007)

docs.title: Reference entry schema (ADR 0007)
docs.text:
One YAML file per paper, docs/references/entries/<id>.yaml.

Field Meaning id <firstauthor><year>-<short> in kebab-case, e.g. hanson2007-spins-rmp; the file name title, authors, year, venue as published doi the DOI (10.xxxx/...); arxiv allowed in addition, never instead, unless the paper has no DOI layers phantom layers the paper informs: layout, electrostatics, disorder, valley, charge, readout, spin provides list of items, see below status proposed (written by a session) or confirmed (a human opened the paper and checked every item) confirmed_by, confirmed_on GitHub handle and date; present only when confirmed notes what the paper does not say, approximations in the comparison, anything a reader should know

Each item in provides:

Field Meaning label stable short label a test names, e.g. fig3b, table1-row2, eq12 kind figure (a digitized curve), table, value, range, formula quantity what it is, with unit in the name or the text, e.g. valley_splitting_ueV conditions material class, temperature, field, dot size: whatever the paper states value, tolerance for value/range; the paper's own uncertainty, or the stated reading precision data for figure/table: path under data/<id>/, a CSV with a header row naming columns and units digitized {method, by, on} for curves read off a figure; extracted for data the paper publishes

Rules: no internal data; a confirmed entry is never edited except to add items, which revert it to proposed until confirmed again; a test may not hard-code a value that lives in the library.

docs.title: Gallery protocols (rendered by CI, signed off per protocol by a human; ADR 0008)
docs.text:
• compiled-device-roundtrip — the coarse map from the compiled and from the reloaded device, and their (zero) difference
  • virtual-gates-map — the coarse map in raw and in virtual plunger coordinates
  • optimum-sensor-flank — the sensor peak and the flank the optimum chooses
  • optimum-coupling-target — t against the barrier gate at the compile tier and from the runtime exponential; the optimum's choice for three targets beside the compile-tier crossing
  • optimum-readout-point — the blockade contrast with the chosen read point; the Elzerman empty probability with the chosen read time
  • optimum-sweet-spot — SWAP infidelity through the chosen sweet spot, and J
  • compiled-device-draws — twelve devices from one layout: coupling, lead rates, sensor rates, valley draws, and what the optimum reaches; devices that do not form are recorded
  • added with the sensor dot's barriers and bath (#47, ADR 0026): sensor-bath-turn-on, sensor-barrier-barrier-map, sensor-barrier-rates, sensor-peak-broadening
  • each carries a budget (ADR 0009); all unsigned

docs.text:
• session-charge-trace — the charge a sample sees at a dot-lead degeneracy at three dwells, and the noisy read at 1 ms
  • session-hold-relaxation — the mean charge after a hold relaxing on exp(−Γ_out t) (every rate out of the held state at the read point), and one trajectory
  • session-closing-barrier — the dots' rates along B_L, a P1 sweep that latches into a loop with B_L closed, and a telegraph trace at the closed transition (#53, ADR 0027)
